messages:
maya: Heads-up: scheduled terraform run tonight 23:00 UTC to merge network egress rules + service-account trust updates. Affects staging/prod. ETA ~20m. Marking release window 23:00-23:30.

deploy-bot: terraform plan completed. Change summary: +3 resources, ~2 modified, 1 destroy. Plan link: https://deploybot.internal/plans/1777778888. State lock: lock-4382.

derek: Who is doing the apply? I can, but @sre-oncall please watch in case we need to roll back. :eyes:

sre-oncall: I'll be on watch. Don't do tfstate moves during the window. If plan shows route table replacement, pause and call me immediately.

chandra: Quick note — I pushed a provider override to the release branch to pin aws provider to 5.12.0 due to behavior changes in 5.13. Can someone confirm the plan reflects the pinned provider?

maya: Plan snippet showing the risky bits:
```
# aws_route.rtb-egress will be replaced, reason: attribute order change
~ resource "aws_route" "rtb-egress" {
    destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
    gateway_id             = "gw-12345" -> "gw-12345"
    # (some attributes changed order)
}
# aws_iam_role.deploy-ci will be updated (policy document change)
```

derek: I see aws_route.rtb-egress marked for replacement because of a description reformat. We should add a lifecycle ignore_changes on description to avoid a replace. I'll push a tiny patch to the branch now.

chandra: If that replacement goes through, flow logs will flap for ~30s. Suggest canary-by-AZ: apply to us-west-2b only, watch 10m, then roll other AZs. Can we do a staged apply with a region/az var?

maya: Yes — deploybot supports staggered applies. We can run: `/deploybot apply --targets=module.network --regions=us-west-2b --stagger=1m` but per runbook that requires two approvers for production. I'll request approval.

ops-runner: I added a short rollback playbook to the runbook: steps are snapshot S3 state, revert branch (git revert), and re-apply previous module version. Also included a quick `terraform state pull` snapshot step and S3 version id capture. Link: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/network-rollback

derek: Also confirm backend snapshot before apply. @maya can you capture the S3 version id and push to the incident thread?

maya: Snapshot created: s3://redwood-tfstate/prod/network.tfstate versionId: v12-1678. Pushed to runbook and release ticket. Starting canary apply in ~10m after approvals.

deploy-bot: Apply initiated by maya at 1777778900. Streaming logs: https://deploybot.internal/applies/1777778900

maya: Canary apply finished — no errors. Observed a ~120ms latency blip on front-door for ~2m, recovered. No 5xx. Continuing to roll to remaining AZs in 2m.

sre-oncall: Watching. No 5xx spikes on infra metrics, but saw a single CloudTrail event for iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy — intended?

chandra: Intentional. We updated infra-ci role to restrict principals to `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-ci-prod`. Verified with policy lint. :white_check_mark:

derek: Proceeding with full roll now. If any route replacement occurs unexpectedly, abort and revert to state version v11. Ops will trigger rollback steps.

deploy-bot: Apply completed at 1777779230. Result: 3 added, 2 modified, 0 deleted. Post-apply checks: network ping OK, flow logs active, CI assume-role verified.

maya: Filing release note: reduced NAT egress CIDR consolidation (cost reduction) + tightened CI assume-role trust for cross-account deploys. PR/RN: RN-287. Thanks all — great coordination :tada:
